correctness.rationale: Van Santen et al. Eqs. (1)–(3) and the uniform one-vertex clock give the displayed kernels exactly on a loopless clique. All p_j>0 for j<N and N is absorbing, so finite blocks give a geometric absorption bound at fixed N. With v=N−j the active nudge down transition exactly cancels the two social terms in p_j−q_j and leaves h; when it is clipped to zero p_j≥hv/N. The conditional drop of H_v is p_j/v−q_j/(v+1)≥h/N. Deterministic-time telescoping followed by the tail-sum formula bounds the mean by NH_v/h. Any successful trajectory must select all initial B vertices, which gives the coupon-collection lower bound; α=1 is pure death at probability Ev/N, giving equality at the upper bound. Rechecked the contextual push proof: the first-step difference products give the full finite formula; all factors above one are precisely those after floor((N−1)E), and they form one summand available for every start. The lower and polynomial-times-upper sandwiches use the same positive-part Riemann sum. The alternative prior-theory comparison changes each fixed-profile positive product term by a bounded factor uniformly (one inverse death rate and at most N−1 ratios), and the Poisson clock changes means by N, so neither changes the log rate per vertex. The endpoint v=N has mean extra wait 1/(Nh) in the comparison chain. All parameter and time-unit hypotheses and the exclusion of initially unanimous A from the logarithmic statement are retained.

evidence: For the push opponent count v the fixed-profile birth/death quotient is (1−x)/[c(1−x)+h] for x=v/N, so the cited superthreshold law gives the exact action integral and uniformity. Finite-N denominators perturb each rate ratio by at most N/(N−1), and the prior nonnegative exact sum therefore absorbs this with at most a bounded factor. For nudging, q_j can vanish on an entire interval and is never large enough to balance p_j at a positive opponent count.

value.rationale: The count kernel includes possible reversions before consensus, so the coupon lower bound alone does not determine their cost. The matching finite upper scale shows that, for this concrete clipped rule and uniform selection, reversions do not change the coupon-collection order from any start, including one dissenter. This supplies a useful quantitative comparison with the known birth–death barrier for the other originally paired rule, in the same time units and for the same field parameters. No independent new value is assigned to the prior push law.
